source: NCERT Class VIII, Our Pasts III, History Ch. 5.

sections.heading: 1. Causes of the Revolt of 1857
points: **Political:** annexations (Doctrine of Lapse — Jhansi, Satara, Nagpur; annexation of **Awadh, 1856**); ending of pensions (e.g. **Nana Saheb**).
**Economic:** heavy taxes, ruin of artisans and peasants.
**Social/Religious:** fear that the British wanted to **convert Indians to Christianity**; interference in customs.

**Military:** discontent among **sepoys** (low pay, poor prospects); the immediate spark was the **greased cartridges** (rumoured to be coated with **cow and pig fat**), offending both Hindus and Muslims.

sections.heading: 2. The Outbreak and Spread
points: **Mangal Pandey** (Barrackpore) fired the first shots (March 1857); the revolt began at **Meerut (10 May 1857)**.
Rebels marched to **Delhi** and proclaimed the aged Mughal emperor **Bahadur Shah Zafar** as their leader.
It spread across north and central India — **Kanpur, Lucknow, Jhansi, Bareilly, Arrah**.

sections.heading: 3. Leaders of 1857
points: **Delhi** — Bahadur Shah Zafar (nominal head), Bakht Khan.
**Kanpur** — **Nana Saheb** and **Tantia Tope**.
**Jhansi** — **Rani Lakshmibai**.
**Lucknow (Awadh)** — **Begum Hazrat Mahal**.
**Bihar (Arrah)** — **Kunwar Singh**.

sections.heading: 4. Suppression and Aftermath
points: The British crushed the revolt by **1858** with great brutality; **Delhi** was recaptured, **Bahadur Shah Zafar exiled to Rangoon (Yangon)**.
**End of the East India Company:** by the **Government of India Act 1858**, India came under the **direct rule of the British Crown**.
**Queen Victoria's Proclamation (1858):** promised no more annexations, respect for princes' rights and religion; the Governor-General became the **Viceroy**.
The **army was reorganised** (more British soldiers, fewer from Awadh/Bihar).

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Immediate cause = greased cartridges (cow & pig fat); Mangal Pandey fired first (Barrackpore).
Revolt began at Meerut, 10 May 1857; rebels rallied around Bahadur Shah Zafar at Delhi.
Leaders: Nana Saheb & Tantia Tope (Kanpur), Rani Lakshmibai (Jhansi), Begum Hazrat Mahal (Lucknow), Kunwar Singh (Arrah).
1858: Company rule ended → British Crown (Govt of India Act 1858); Queen's Proclamation; Viceroy created.
Bahadur Shah Zafar exiled to Rangoon.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: The revolt started at **Meerut on 10 May 1857**; **Mangal Pandey's** act was earlier at **Barrackpore**.
**Rani Lakshmibai = Jhansi; Nana Saheb/Tantia Tope = Kanpur; Begum Hazrat Mahal = Lucknow.**
After 1857, the **Government of India Act 1858** transferred power to the **Crown** (end of the Company).
The **Governor-General** was now also titled **Viceroy**.
